tools.description:
Find a tool on OpenSea's registry that actually works. The registry holds roughly ten thousand tools and single publishers have listed hundreds each in bulk, so name-matching alone hands you a dead endpoint. This ranks matches by unique paying callers and real paid calls, flags never-used and bulk-published listings, and returns each one's price and OpenSea link. Measured from OpenSea's own payment records — no editorial, no paid placement.

HOW TO CALL IT: POST {"task": "check whether an ERC-20 token is a honeypot"}. Options: "maxPriceUsd", "provenOnly" (default true) and "limit" (default 8). YOU GET BACK matching tools ranked by whether anyone actually uses them, each with its OpenSea URL, its real price and a trust score out of 100. WHY YOU NEED IT: the registry holds roughly ten thousand tools and single publishers have listed hundreds each in bulk. Almost none have ever been called. Name-matching alone will hand you a dead endpoint. HOW IT RANKS: unique paying callers first, then total paid calls, then price, then how heavily that one domain has bulk-published. Measured from OpenSea's own payment records — no model, no editorial, no paid placement. FLAGS TO READ: `never-used` means nobody has ever paid for it, `bulk-publisher` means the domain floods the registry, `unpriced` means it advertises no readable price. LIMITS: read-only discovery. It does not call, pay or vet the tools it finds, and usage is evidence, not a safety guarantee.
